CHIEF COMPLAINT
Dysphagia and chest pain with swallowing.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Raymond presents with a several-week history of difficulty swallowing with associated chest pain, particularly with larger pieces of food. Pain is not present with every meal but occurs with most foods. He reports that bigger pieces of food feel like they are getting stuck. He denies weight loss and reports recent weight gain of approximately 10 pounds over the past month. He attributes recent dietary changes (pizza, burgers) to increased stress from relocating from the west coast to the east coast. He also reports occasional epigastric pain. Denies nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Denies hematochezia or melena.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for epigastric discomfort. Negative for fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, hematochezia, or melena.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not documented.

MEDICATIONS
Not documented at time of visit.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is currently relocating from west coast to east coast, which he describes as stressful. He is planning to drive rather than fly due to concerns about pet travel. Recent increase in consumption of fast food including pizza and burgers. Uses alcohol and caffeine.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: BP 133/70, HR normal, afebrile, RR 19, O2 sat 100%. Weight gain of 10 lbs noted over past month.
HEENT: No oral ulcers, no thrush, tonsils midline. Neck: No lymphadenopathy, no thyromegaly.
Abdomen: Nondistended with active bowel sounds. Pain to palpation in epigastric area. Negative Murphy's sign, no peritoneal signs, no rebound tenderness.
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Skin: No rash, lesions, or bruising.
Eyes: Equal and reactive to light.

RESULTS
Barium swallow study: Two areas of mild narrowing in the mid and lower portions of the esophagus consistent with esophagitis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Acute esophagitis. Prescribed Protonix 40 mg once daily in the morning to reduce gastric acid production. Prescribed Carafate 1 gram four times daily for one month to coat the esophageal and gastric lining. Patient counseled to decrease alcohol and caffeine intake, avoid citrus fruits and spicy foods until symptoms improve, eat slowly, and chew food more thoroughly. Upper endoscopy scheduled for next week to rule out other pathology. Follow-up appointment scheduled for next week.
